body:
HOLD ADDRESSED. Revised candidate f849104 on m1/chart-eligibility, base 234dd09 (current main,
rebased and re-gated on it, not carried across). Supersedes 460a14a.

YOUR FINDING WAS RIGHT AND I ACCEPT IT WITHOUT QUALIFICATION. structuralEligible now requires a
configured provider AND unit evidence AND at least one charted structural member. Both terms are
produced by reductions over the same structuralMembers population, and now both eligibility
predicates consult it - a single `chartedMembers` val they share, so they cannot drift apart again.

I reproduced your court exactly. The mutation, reverting only structuralEligible to its pre-fix
form, fails the new law with your numbers to the digit:
  expected 0.9552238805970149 but was 0.8311688311688312
thirteen siblings passing.

BOTH LAWS YOU ASKED FOR ARE IN:
  "a configured structural provider is inert on a chartless cell"        - the court
  "a configured structural provider is not inert where the source is charted" - the control
The second is there for the reason you would have raised next: "a configured provider is inert" is
satisfiable by ignoring the provider everywhere, which would be a worse bug than the one being
fixed. It asserts the term IS present and the total DOES move when the source is charted.

E198 fixed - the unused CheckState.Checked is gone. The chart fixture is hoisted to suite level so
the chartless and charted views are built from the same evidence and differ only in where it is
attached; that is what makes the pair a matched comparison rather than two unrelated setups.

WHAT I TAKE FROM THIS. The comment at that very site already said, in my own words, that treating an
impossible measurement as a missed one "would invent a dimension that cell cannot have". I wrote
that warning about Chart and left Structural doing exactly it, in the same expression, four lines
down. Finding one half of a symmetry is not finding the symmetry, and I stopped at the half that
had a failing number attached. The two defects also point opposite ways - Chart discounted coarse
anchors, Structural inflated chartless ones - so neither would have surfaced the other by making
some aggregate look wrong.

Gate: seven modules via reference-scope.sh, seven totals counted, zero failures - align 211,
codec 108, embedBench 64, embedGrakern 28, fixtures 117, interview 92, laws 86. scalafmtCheckAll
last, clean. The 211 excludes my scratch probes; they are untracked and emptied, not committed.

Ready for your re-review. I still hold cost.scala (rv-01M17N8HH49AH9NQTK2MV4CS0T) and
CostSuite.scala (rv-01M17M70JNTR5M0G2GXM6QTFKP), nothing else.

One separate thing, not part of this candidate and not a request to act: while waiting on your
review I probed UnbalancedSinkhorn and a single fully-excluded row - costs at Double.MaxValue/4,
exactly what CostBreakdown.unassessable prices a cell at - zeroes the ENTIRE transport plan, good
rows included, while solve returns Right. Control at cost 50 gives the good row 1.223 mass. It has
no production caller today so nothing is corrupted; I sent the probe to cursor-grok-4.6 who holds
that file, and to chief. Flagging it here only because the input that triggers it is the exclusion
carrier from this bead.
